text.p: Hurricane Hortense remains as a strong risk to shipping as it moves from the southeast Bahamas islands east of the central Bahamas islands during today and early Friday. Top winds near the center of the system are about 115 mph with some further flucuations of strength over the next 24 hours. Hortense will also cause heavy rains and strong winds through the islands in the area with property damage due to these winds, flooding and mudslides. Hortense pulls away from the Bahamas later Friday and tracks northward parallel to the East Coast of the USA.

Tropical depression 24w continues fairly weak in the western South China Sea near Hainan, China. This system is only a minor risk to shipping but could bring some locally heavy rains to Hainan Island. Some slight intensification is expected this period.

Tropical depression 25W has formed east of Guam. Top winds are near 30 mph and strengthening is expected this period as the storm likely becomes a Tropical Storm and possibly a Typhoon as the system tracks northwestward.
Tropical depression 26W has formed in the Philippine Sea. Slight intensification is expected this period. TD26W is a minor threat to shipping.

Hurricane Fausto is mainly a risk to shipping in the region from well west of Manzanillo Mexico to just southwest of Baja. Top winds near the center of Fausto are now about 85 mph but they may increase to about 100-110 mph in about 24 hours. Rain along the coast of west Mexico and south Baja may be enough to cause some locally flooding. The strongest winds should stay off shore but some high gusts are still possible along the coast.
